candidates.statement: For the platform technology designation program, section 506K of the FD&C Act establishes 35 criteria outlining who can request designations and who, once that platform technology has been 36 designated, can leverage them. This guidance describes those categories and provides 37 recommendations for the types of platform technologies that may be eligible for consideration 38 for designation. This guidance also gives recommendations for what should be included in 39 submission requests to designate a platform technology, how to update a designated platform 40 technology and, when appropriate, the process for revoking a designation. 41

candidates.statement: If FDA has approved an Abbreviated New Drug Application (ANDA), New Drug Application 51 (NDA), or Biologics License Application (BLA) for a drug that incorporates or uses a platform 52 technology as defined in section 506K(h)(1) of the FD&C Act, a sponsor of a subsequent 53 Investigational New Drug (IND), NDA, or 351(a) BLA can request designation of that platform 54 technology to enable leveraging of the technology in new or future applications. 7 FDA 55 recommends requesting the designation of a platform technology during the IND phase of drug 56 development for a planned subsequent NDA or 351(a) BLA, because by this stage of 57 development, the sponsor should have sufficient knowledge to outline for FDA how the 58

To support a designation, this 128 information must sufficiently demonstrate the potential for the platform technology to be 129 incorporated in, or used by, the drug(s) under investigation without adversely affecting quality, 130 manufacturing, or safety. 17 For example, if the sponsor wants to leverage stability testing, the 131 preliminary evidence should demonstrate the similarities in the molecule, the manufacturing 132 process 18 such that leveraging stability data would be justified. candidates.statement: Sponsors can request the designation of a platform technology at any time concurrent with or 297 after the submission of an IND. Any platform technology designation request should be made in 298 accordance with the electronic submission guidelines. 25 Although a sponsor can request 299 designation concurrent with the submission of an IND, the timing of the request for designation 300 should consider whether there are adequate product-specific data. FDA recommends the sponsor 301 submit far enough into their development cycle to permit a determination of suitability for 302 platform technology designation (e.g., of whether the platform technology has the potential to be 303 incorporated in, or used by, more than one drug without an adverse effect on quality, 304 manufacturing, or safety). 26 The sponsor’s submission should clearly indicate in the 305 administrative documents in Module 1 that it is a request for a platform technology designation. 306 The submission should also contain the following information in Module 1: 307

Although a sponsor can request designation concurrent with the submission of an IND, 334 FDA recommends that the sponsor submit far enough into their development cycle of the product 335 to permit a determination of suitability for platform technology designation. 28 Any designation 336 requests that are submitted at the same time as a new IND or a subsequent IND amendment will 337 be evaluated separately from the safety assessment of the new IND or of any subsequent IND 338 amendments (e.g., a proposed new clinical protocol, a Chemistry, Manufacturing, and Controls 339 (CMC) or Pharmacology/Toxicology amendment). 29 FDA will determine whether the 340 designation meets the eligibility factors and if the platform technology will be designated within 341

candidates.statement: For a technology to be designated, it must not only meet the platform technology definition in 436 the statute, but it must also meet the eligibility factors for designation under 506(K)(b). It is 437 possible, therefore, for a technology to meet the definition of a platform technology under 438 506K(h) but not be designated by FDA as a designated platform technology. For example, a 439 technology that meets the definition of a platform technology might be inappropriate for the 440 designation program because current review processes already reflect the use of the well- 441 understood technology or there is a public standard. Therefore, FDA would not consider such 442 technologies to meet the criterion of bringing significant efficiencies to the drug development, 443 manufacturing, and review processes for the purposes of the designated platform technology 444 program. Examples of technologies that could be inappropriate for the designation program 445 because the technologies do not meet the definition, criteria, or both, include the following: 446
